skill.name: reviewing-code
skill.description: Guides structured code reviews with local checks, review categories, and clear approval verdicts.
skill.summary: Review pull requests with repeatable checks and a consistent verdict format.
skill.author: BPSAI

security_audit.summary: Five static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fence delimiters, not executable Ruby or shell backticks. One finding is confirmed because the documented xargs pipeline consumes repository-controlled filenames without null delimiting or an option terminator. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Unsafe xargs use over changed filenames
remediation.suggestion: Use null-delimited filenames and an option terminator, such as git diff -z with xargs -0 and grep --.

finding_verdicts.reason: The finding points to a Markdown code fence delimiter, not Ruby backtick execution. The enclosed commands are fixed review helpers with no user-controlled shell interpolation.
The snippet is the closing Markdown fence for the previous command block. It is documentation syntax and cannot execute code by itself.
The snippet starts a Markdown example block for the review output format. It is not shell syntax or dynamic code execution.
The snippet is a closing Markdown fence for a formatting example. No command is present at this location.
The finding is triggered by a Markdown bash fence, not Ruby backtick execution. The commands inside are documented checks with fixed programs and no shell substitution.

The command pipes repository-controlled filenames into xargs grep without null delimiters or an option terminator. Malicious or unusual filenames can make the check unreliable and can alter grep behavior.

medium_findings.title: xargs command (can execute arbitrary commands)
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command pipes repository-controlled filenames into xargs grep without null delimiters or an option terminator. Malicious or unusual filenames can make the check unreliable and can alter grep behavior.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes with Structured Checks
content.value_statement: Code changes can miss tests, secrets, and review structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through repeatable checks and concise review output.
actual_capabilities: Provides quick commands for CI, project validation, and git diff inspection.
Defines a review format with summary, required fixes, suggestions, positive notes, and verdict.
Checks public functions for type hints, docstrings, tests, and existing project patterns.
Prompts reviewers to look for hardcoded values and unmocked external services.
Includes grep-based checks for debug statements, TODO markers, and possible secrets in diffs.
limitations: Assumes bpsai-pair, git, grep, and xargs are available in the environment.
Uses main...HEAD as the default comparison range.
Text searches can miss complex issues and may produce false positives.
Does not replace maintainer judgment or project-specific security review.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent review format before approving or requesting changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Changes for Review
use_cases.description: Run local quality checks and remove obvious issues before submitting code.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reviews
use_cases.description: Give reviewers a shared checklist for tests, configuration, public interfaces, and secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Change Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current changes using the reviewing-code skill. Focus on must-fix issues, tests, and clear approval guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this branch before I open a pull request. Run the recommended local checks and summarize blockers first.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the diff for hardcoded secrets, unsafe external service usage, missing tests, and unmocked integrations. Separate must-fix items from optional improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Release Gate Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this branch as a release gate. Include CI status, validation results, risk areas, and a final approval recommendation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before merge or release.

output_examples.input: A contributor asks for review of a feature branch before opening a pull request.
output: Summary: The change is close, but tests are missing for the new public path.
Must Fix: Add tests for the new behavior and remove the debug output.
Verdict: Request changes until the missing tests and debug output are resolved.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks whether a small bug fix can be approved.
output: Summary: The fix is narrow and follows existing project patterns.
Should Fix: Add one regression test if time permits.
Verdict: Approve with comments because the risk is low.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead wants the same review structure across a team.
output: Summary: The review uses shared categories for blockers, suggestions, and positive notes.
Must Fix: Confirm CI and validation results before approval.
Verdict: Use the same approval options for every reviewed change.

best_practices: Run the CI and validation commands before writing the final review.
Separate must-fix issues from optional improvements.
Cite files and lines when reporting review findings.
anti_patterns: Do not approve changes when tests for new behavior are missing.
Do not treat grep results as complete secret scanning.
Do not run suggested commands without checking the repository and branch context.

faq.question: What tools does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects git plus project tools such as bpsai-pair, grep, and xargs when running the listed checks.

faq.question: Can it review any programming language?
faq.answer: It can structure reviews for many repositories, but project-specific checks are focused on Python-style public interfaces.

faq.question: Does it make approval decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the review and asks for an explicit verdict based on evidence.

faq.question: Can it find secrets reliably?
faq.answer: No. It uses simple diff searches and should be paired with a dedicated secret scanner.

faq.question: Does it change files?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes review commands and output format. Any file changes come from the user or agent actions.

faq.question: How should teams customize it?
faq.answer: Teams should adjust the branch range, required checks, and project-specific review rules to match their workflow.
